title: Which temperature in Leh goes with which time?
description: Four readings in Leh on a November day, two above zero and two below, are matched with four times. The two readings above zero go with the daytime and the two below zero with the night, and the lower reading goes with the later, colder hour. Each match is checked against the order of the readings.
teaching_notes: One idea: order the four readings from the highest to the lowest, then order the times from the warmest part of the day to the coldest part of the night. Watch for students who match minus four with the warmer time because four is a bigger number than two.

video_script.why: The child orders four readings, two positive and two negative, and matches them with the times of a cold November day in Leh.
video_script.substitution: The book's own table of four temperatures and four times for Leh in Ladakh.
video_script.anchor: a thermometer scale beside a clock, for Leh in Ladakh on a November day
video_script.payoff_line: The lower reading belongs to the colder hour, and a negative reading is lower than a positive one.

final_answer.spoken: fourteen degrees at two in the afternoon, eight degrees at eleven in the morning, minus two degrees at eleven at night, and minus four degrees at two in the night

maths_rules: readings: 14, 8, -2, -4 (degrees Celsius); order from highest to lowest: 14 > 8 > -2 > -4
a negative reading is lower than any positive reading; among negatives, -4 is lower than -2
the sun warms the day: 02:00 p.m. is the warmest of the four times and 11:00 a.m. is warm but cooler
after sunset the air cools: 11:00 p.m. is cold and 02:00 a.m. is later in the night, so colder still
matches: 14 with 02:00 p.m., 8 with 11:00 a.m., -2 with 11:00 p.m., -4 with 02:00 a.m. (book's answer key)
video_script.design: A thermometer scale with four marks, teal above zero and amber below. A clock beside it shows the four times. Lines join each reading to its time.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a snowy town with a thermometer and a clock beside it, and four temperature cards waiting to be matched

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.town: the snowy town of Leh appears with a thermometer and a clock
marks.cards: the four temperature cards and the four time cards appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the town of Leh in Ladakh.
<bookmark mark='town'/>Leh gets very cold in winter, and four readings were taken on a day in November.
<bookmark mark='cards'/>Each reading belongs to one time of the day or night.
Which reading goes with which time?

beats.on_screen: the thermometer, the clock and the cards stay on the board
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a tall thermometer scale; 0 marked as the freezing point of water; teal above 0 labelled positive, amber below 0 labelled negative; an arrow shows higher means warmer

marks.zero: the 0 mark lights up and is labelled freezing point of water
marks.up: an arrow shows that higher means warmer

beats.colours: above zero teal, below zero amber
narration: <bookmark mark='scale'/>A thermometer scale is like a number line standing upright.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>Zero degrees Celsius is the freezing point of water.
<bookmark mark='up'/>The higher the level, the warmer it is. A negative reading is lower than a positive one.

marks.given: the four readings and the four times are written in two columns

beats.colours: teal for plus, amber for minus
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four readings and four times from a day in November.

beats.on_screen: To find: the time that goes with each reading

marks.find: an arrow joins the two columns

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the time that goes with each reading.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: order the readings from the highest to the lowest: 14, 8, -2, -4

marks.order: the four readings line up on the scale from the top down
marks.neg: the two negative readings sit below the 0 mark

beats.colours: teal for plus, amber for minus
narration: <bookmark mark='order'/>Step one, order the readings from the highest to the lowest.
Fourteen is the highest, then eight, then minus two, and minus four is the lowest.
<bookmark mark='neg'/>The two negative readings are lower than the two positive ones.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: day or night: the two positive readings go with the daytime, 02:00 p.m. and 11:00 a.m.; the two negative readings go with the night, 11:00 p.m. and 02:00 a.m.

marks.day: a sun is drawn over 02:00 p.m. and 11:00 a.m.
marks.pos: the two positive readings are joined to the sun
marks.night: a moon is drawn over 11:00 p.m. and 02:00 a.m.

beats.colours: teal for day, amber for night
narration: <bookmark mark='day'/>Step two, split the times into day and night.
The sun warms the day.
<bookmark mark='pos'/>The two positive readings go with two in the afternoon and eleven in the morning.
<bookmark mark='night'/>The two negative readings go with eleven at night and two in the night.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the day: 02:00 p.m. is warmer than 11:00 a.m., so 14 °C goes with 02:00 p.m. and 8 °C goes with 11:00 a.m.
narration: <bookmark mark='pm'/>Step three, match the daytime pair.
Two in the afternoon is warmer than eleven in the morning.
<bookmark mark='am'/>Fourteen degrees goes with two in the afternoon, and eight degrees goes with eleven in the morning.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: the night: 02:00 a.m. is later in the night and colder than 11:00 p.m., so -4 °C goes with 02:00 a.m. and -2 °C goes with 11:00 p.m.
narration: <bookmark mark='late'/>Step four, match the night pair.
Two in the night comes later, after the air has cooled for hours, so it is colder.
<bookmark mark='early'/>Minus four degrees goes with two in the night, and minus two degrees goes with eleven at night.

beats.on_screen: Step 5, check: the readings 14, 8, -2, -4 fall in the same order as the times 02:00 p.m., 11:00 a.m., 11:00 p.m., 02:00 a.m., from the warmest to the coldest

marks.check: the two lists are placed side by side
marks.lines: the lines between them are drawn and do not cross

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check the order.
From the warmest time to the coldest time, the readings go down in the same order.
<bookmark mark='lines'/>The lines between the two lists do not cross.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The lower reading belongs to the colder hour, and a negative reading is lower than a positive one.
<bookmark mark='day'/>Fourteen degrees is at two in the afternoon, and eight degrees is at eleven in the morning.
<bookmark mark='night'/>Minus two degrees is at eleven at night, and minus four degrees is at two in the night.
